newsitem.title: USA: Alex. Brown had Q1 decline in M&A, IPOs.
newsitem.headline: Alex. Brown had Q1 decline in M&A, IPOs.

text.p: Alex. Brown Inc said Thursday lower revenue from merger and advisory fees and a slimmer new issue equity calendar contributed to a 26 percent decline in investment banking revenue to $74.9 million in the first quarter of 1997.
Overall, revenue fell 14 percent to $233.5 milliion, net income fell 23 percent to $31.2 million, and earnings per share diluted fell 26 percent to $1.10 from $1.48.
On April 6, Alex. Brown and Bankers Trust New York Corp announced a definitive merger agreement. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 1997.

Alex. Brown said principal transaction revenue fell 39 percent to $32.0 million due mainly to decreases in equity trading. The company said the decrease was representative of market volatility during the first quarter.

"Our first quarter results are reflective of the tempestuous swings in the equity markets and resultant reduced underwriting activity," said A. B. Krongard, chairman and chief executive, in a statement. "In spite of this volatility, we were able to produce a solid quarter, principally due to exceptional efforts by our employees and the balance among our businesses."

Alex. Brown recorded a 12 percent increase in $58.2 million, mainly due to increased institutional and private client business and the mutual fund business. Interest and dividend income rose eight percent to $35.7 million due to growth in margin loans in the private client business. As of March 31, margin balances totaled $1.6 billion, an increase of nine percent from a year ago.
The first quarter's $1.10 per share diluted earnings compared to a consensus estimate of $1.33, analysts siad.
Alex. Brown shares were up one to 60 at midday. Bankers Trust, which earlier Thursday reported better-than-expected earnings of $1.89 per share, was up 1-3/8 to 76-3/8.
